correctness.rationale: For all primes p>=3, d>=2, m>=1 and lambda!=0,1, affineness of all set-map endomorphisms follows from invertible T and 1-T. Direct-summand classification over the local ring R gives exactly one orbit for each free rank r, with N_r derived by GL_m(R) orbit-stabilizer and |ker P|. Commutativity with (P,0) forces the linear part block diagonal and translation in im P, giving Z_r. Their exponent differences factor as (r-t)(2(r+t)-2m+1), whose second factor is never zero. Mixed-block failure uses inequivalent R2 and R1^2 image modules and identical p^8 centralizers. A standalone exhaustive small-ring checker rechecked projections, matrix commutants, explicit quandle homomorphisms and mixed-block linear equations; finite tests are corroboration rather than general proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The underlying finite Alexander quandle can be recast as an affine module over F_p[t,t^{-1}], and its retractions as affine splittings. This recasting does not transfer the semisimple formula: here the nilpotent part of T is nonzero and centralizing units form GL_m(F_p[epsilon]/epsilon^d), rather than a product of matrix groups over fields. Neither inspected quandle-equivalence theorem gives conjugacy-class centralizer sizes for this nonsemisimple case.

value.rationale: The endomorphism composition-centralizer cardinality unexpectedly becomes a complete invariant of full automorphism-conjugacy among all quandle retractions, uniformly over nonsemisimple repeated Jordan blocks, while equal-size centralizer information fails on a nearby four-dimensional mixed-block module. Exact labeled and centralizer counts give a natural complete census, a commuting-pair number, and a precise structural scope boundary; this is not only a routine special-case linear centralizer evaluation.
